papers.title: Pricing of Climate Risk Insurance: Regulation and Cross-Subsidies
papers.abstract: Insurers overcome regulatory frictions by cross-subsidizing insurance across states, leading to a decoupling of rates from underlying risk.

papers.title: Climate Capitalists
papers.abstract: Green firms & divisions report lower perceived cost of capital and discount rates in recent years, concurrent with the rise of "green investing."

papers.title: Democratizing Private Markets? Private Equity Performance of Individual Investors
papers.abstract: Individual investors match institutional PE performance, but advisor skill and fee layers drive sharp return disparities across households.

papers.title: Green Price Pressure
papers.abstract: We study the catering channel of sustainable investing: managers improve environmental performance to capture valuation premia created by investor demand for sustainability.

papers.title: Limited Risk Transfer Between Investors: A New Benchmark for Macro-Finance Models
papers.abstract: Risk transfer (how much risk changes hands) is small: 0.65% per quarter. Standard models, however, predict 10x more. A new model with inelastic demand provides reconciliation.

papers.title: Rating Without Market Discipline
papers.abstract: We show that private ratings for opaque debt held by life insurers systematically understate credit risk, lower required capital, and reveal the limits of regulation when market discipline is absent.

papers.title: Social Inflation
papers.abstract: I uncover a new source of aggregate risk for the insurance sector: shifts in insurers' loss distribution induced by changing social norms and legal developments.

papers.title: Cross-sectional Skewness
papers.abstract: We evaluate the skewness in the cross-section of returns in light of predictions from a well-known class of asset pricing models.
